journeys.name: b5-telex-main-flow
journeys.note: generalTelexPat (数据报/电传组训) full lifecycle on a fixed 12-group digit cable floor with frontend payloads (telexZuXun list.js add, student.vue detail {trainId,userId}, datagramTrain.js getPage/startTrain/uploadResult{patValue,protocolVersion,attempt,captureIntervals}/finish, teacher.js updateTrainStatus + WS begin/end). Teacher sweep-admin (creator, role 1) connects to the room BEFORE the students so getOnline order exposes Java students-first/teacher-last. Student1 text has one wrong group and a missing last group, then an extension adds the missing group (patGroup 13, errorCode 1 -> Java accuracy 92.00 vs Rust 92.31). Covers 207/208/202 precedence incl. outsider startTrain/finish (Java 207), WS error frames, classic-socket 200/201 notices vs room-socket fan-out, statistics, patDetail/getPage/getPatValue after settlement, delete closing sockets. Determinism: cable content fixed; upload intervals fixed [0,400]/[450,700] with a 1.0 s sleep after start (bound = server elapsed); only serverElapsedMs, ids and the ended-training validTime (wall clock) are masked; userInfoList/userTendencyVO unordered because Java queries have no ORDER BY and member ids are random UUIDs. No telex reset endpoint exists in Java.

journeys.name: b5-telex-two-page-settlement-and-fanout
journeys.note: Two-floor cable (100 groups + 3 groups, totalNumber 200) settled by the student; page 1 has >=100 groups and no '-' page mark, page 2 has 3 groups. Java checks the page mark per page (TelexPatUtils.java:130, groupNumber) and treats a missing dash as lessPage; Rust uses the cumulative patGroup (general_train.rs:2787) and a no-dash digit prefix as errorPage -> deductInfo lessPageNumber/errorPageNumber differ (rule lessPage 7 vs errorPage 3). After finish getPage page 1 / getPatValue / patDetail show whether analysis rows (sort>=0) exist (Java yes, Rust never writes them). A second non-cable random-content training (type 0 patType 2, total 250, content masked) is created while the student sits in the first room: Java sends the 200 notice only to the classic /websocket socket, Rust also pushes it to the room socket. findPage page 3 before/after finish and patDetail.existPage expose Rust ensure_settlement_pages generating missing pages. Determinism: fixed tokens 1000..1099 / 2000..2002, fixed intervals [0,400]/[450,800] after a 1.2 s sleep; random keys and ids masked; wall-clock serverElapsedMs masked. Speed is intentionally huge (few hundred ms); both stacks must still agree.

journeys.name: b5-telex-rule-and-status-edges
journeys.note: Telex-only edges, each on its own training so a Java divergence does not cascade. D: zero-coefficient rule (wpm r=l=0): Java still emits speedScore '+0'/'-0' (GeneralTelexPatService.java:970-974), Rust omits the key when the adjustment is 0 (general_train.rs:2874); plus an extra trailing line (Java muchLessLine +size-rowNum=2, Rust +1, TelexPatUtils.java:438 vs general_train.rs:2784, suspected). H: cable totalNumber 150 (1 page): Java settles an empty submission, Rust ensure_settlement_pages wants 2 pages and returns 202 '固定报底页不存在'. E: rule created like the telex rule UI (TelexGradeRule.vue:258, no alterError): Java finish dereferences getOther().getAlterError() -> NPE -> HTTP 500 (GeneralTelexPatService.java:940), Rust returns 200 with correctMistakes deduction 0; this training stays unsettled in Java (status 1, so the recovery task does not touch it) and is deleted at the end. F: Java updateStatus has no state machine (accepts 2 before start, restart, status 5); Rust answers 208/202. Expected: several steps differ by design; use them as registry decisions, not as Rust-only regressions.
